pageType: dedicated (country page)
description: One of the world's biggest wine producers. Most vineyards sit at the base of the Andes, where lots of sun and snowmelt irrigation give plump, deep-coloured wines; Malbec is the most important grape.
climate: Sunny and dry at the foot of the Andes, irrigated by snowmelt; cool nights at high elevation
fact: Vineyards reach upwards of 7,500 ft, and the cool nights there help the wines keep their acidity.

video.title: Get To Know Argentina Wine | Wine Folly

pageType: dedicated (Argentina region guide)
description: Argentina's largest wine region and the one with the most wineries. The province is nearly the size of Illinois, holds 75% of the country's vineyards and is ideal for bold reds.
climate: Hot, sunny and very dry (under 9 in. of rain a year) in the Andes rain shadow; snowmelt irrigation
fact: More Malbec is planted in Mendoza than anywhere else in the world.

video.title: Argentina Malbec History and Producers Part 1

pageType: section 'Valle de Uco' of the Mendoza guide page
description: Some of Mendoza's highest vineyards, known for elegant, age-worthy wines. Sub-areas: Tupungato, Tunuyán (Vista Flores) and San Carlos (Paraje Altamira).
climate: High altitude (up to about 5,250 ft in Tupungato), so cooler
fact: Gualtallary, an unofficial area in Tupungato with calcareous soils, is well known among collectors.

video.title: France vs Argentina Malbec Wine

pageType: section 'Luján de Cuyo' of the Mendoza guide page
description: Home to many ultra-modern wineries and boutique hotels. Its Malbec leans to black fruit and Asian spice, with a dusty or graphite-like finish.
fact: Wines are often labelled by town: Agrelo (elegance and power), Vistalba (minerality), Las Compuertas (elegance), Perdriel (tannin).

video.title: Argentina Malbec History and Producers Part 2

pageType: listing page with no editorial text (thin)
section 'Patagonia Pinot Noir' of the Argentina country page
description: An up-and-coming frontier in Argentine wine, with its own take on Pinot Noir from Neuquén and Río Negro.
fact: Patagonian Pinot Noir balances sweet red fruit with leafy, herbal tea-like flavours.

video.title: Pinot Noir (Everything you need to know) | Grapes 101

pageType: dedicated (country page)
description: A thin strip between the Pacific and the Andes with a wide range of styles. Early French investment pushed it toward Bordeaux varieties, and in the 1990s much of its 'Merlot' turned out to be Carménère.
climate: Pacific 'air conditioner'; cool coastal, warm inland valley and mountain zones
fact: Chile's vineyards have not been affected by phylloxera.

video.title: How Well Do You Know Sauvignon Blanc From Chile?

pageType: section 'Maipo' of the Chilean Cabernet article
description: Follows the Maipo river south of Santiago. Its sweet spot, Alto Maipo at the base of the Andes, makes full-bodied red blends reminiscent of Napa Cabernet.
climate: More Mediterranean, cooled by ocean winds
fact: Viña Carmen made the first single-varietal Carménère.

video.title: Cabernet Sauvignon (Everything You Need To Know) | Grapes 101

pageType: section 'Colchagua' of the Chilean Cabernet article
description: Prime Bordeaux-variety vineyards from San Fernando to Santa Cruz. Its Apalta sub-area is known for age-worthy Bordeaux-style blends.
fact: Casa Silva has its own Carménère clone garden in its Los Lingues vineyard.

video.title: Carménère: Bordeaux's Lost Grape

pageType: section 'Aconcagua' of the Chilean Cabernet article
description: Stretches from the coast inland. The Bordeaux-variety zone around Llay Lay, San Felipe and Los Andes makes some of Chile's most structured, tannic reds.
climate: One of Chile's sunniest, driest regions; cool nights
fact: Its blends often show dried berries, minerality and spice notes of red pepper, paprika and black tea.

video.title: Cabernet Sauvignon (Everything You Need To Know) | Grapes 101

pageType: dedicated (country page)
description: Nearly 340,000 acres of vines, known above all for Shiraz and for an industry that keeps innovating.
climate: Warm and dry
fact: Nearly all Australian wines, even super-premium bottles, are sealed with screw caps.

video.title: Are you curious about Australian Shiraz? | Wine Unpacked

pageType: section of the South Australia article
description: One of Australia's oldest and best-known regions. Its Shiraz is among the most powerful in the world: ripe blackberry, dried currant, mocha, tobacco and an earthy note.
climate: Warm and sunny; alcohol often 14–15%
fact: Barossa Valley has Shiraz vines more than 100 years old.

video.title: Are you curious about Australian Shiraz? | Wine Unpacked

pageType: section 'Fleurieu' of the South Australia article
description: Mostly Shiraz in the rolling hills around McLaren Vale: dark and rich, with licorice, roast meat, mocha and graphite.
climate: Hot and dry
fact: Alcohol can naturally reach about 15–16%.

video.title: Are you curious about Australian Shiraz? | Wine Unpacked

pageType: section 'Coonawarra Cabernet' of the Australia country page
description: Its best Cabernet grows on dusty red clay soils, giving depth, powerful tannins and a subtle dried-herb quality.
climate: Cooler than Bordeaux (per the page)
fact: Flavour notes: blackberry, black currant, cedar, spearmint, bay leaf.

video.title: Cabernet Sauvignon (Everything You Need To Know) | Grapes 101

pageType: dedicated (region guide)
description: Called the most isolated wine region in the world, 3 hours south of Perth. In about 50 years it became a world-class producer of Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay.
climate: Mediterranean, ocean-cooled
fact: Margaret River is phylloxera-free and most vines grow on their own roots.

video.title: Margaret River Region Guide: Everything you need to know

pageType: section 'Hunter Valley Sémillon' of the Australia country page
description: Australia's oldest continually operating wine region, outside Sydney, known for Shiraz and Sémillon.
fact: Its Sémillon is lean and minerally: lime, lilac, Asian pear, green pineapple, candle wax.

pageType: section of the Victoria article
description: Red volcanic soils and sandy loam give very different wines, from Bordeaux-like Cabernet to Pinot Noir and delicate Chardonnay.
fact: The lineup includes cult-favourite single-vineyard Nebbiolo.

video.title: Chardonnay (everything you need to know) | Grapes 101

pageType: section of the South Australia article
description: Arguably some of Australia's finest dry Riesling, plus elegant, savoury Cabernet and Cabernet-Merlot.
climate: Greener than the hotter, drier Barossa
fact: Famous Riesling sites include Watervale and Polish Hill River.

video.title: Riesling (Everything you need to know) | Grapes 101

pageType: section of the South Australia article
description: Part of Barossa, higher in the Mount Lofty Ranges. Elevation gives tart, high-acid, age-worthy wines and much of Barossa's white wine.
climate: Cooler than Barossa Valley because of elevation
fact: Henschke's Hill of Grace, one of Australia's most famous single-vineyard wines, is made here.

video.title: Riesling (Everything you need to know) | Grapes 101

pageType: section 'Tasmanian Wines' of the Australia country page
description: A new frontier focused on cool-climate Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and sparkling wines that are lean and smoky.
climate: Cool climate
fact: Tasmania is less than 0.5% of Australia's grape harvest.

video.title: Learn by Tasting (ep. 6) Wine Folly

pageType: dedicated (country page)
description: 10 wine regions across the islands. Called the 'Sauvignon Blanc capital of the world', and strong in cool-climate grapes.
climate: Cool climate
fact: 98% of vineyards meet the ISO 14001 sustainability standard.

video.title: Pinot Noir… From New Zealand? | Wine Folly

pageType: dedicated article
description: Famous for Sauvignon Blanc, now also world-class Pinot Noir. Subregions Wairau Valley, Southern Valleys and Awatere Valley give distinct styles.
climate: Cool, warm days and cool nights
fact: Until the late 1990s most Marlborough Pinot went into sparkling wine.

video.title: Sauvignon Blanc (Everything you need to know) | Grapes 101

pageType: section of the NZ Chardonnay article
description: The world's southernmost wine region, best known for Pinot Noir; also tightly structured Chardonnay.
climate: Dry and mountainous; cool nights, long sunlight hours
fact: Chardonnay here ripens at lower sugar levels while keeping high acidity.

video.title: Pinot Noir… From New Zealand? | Wine Folly

pageType: dedicated article
description: A warm, maritime region on the North Island's east coast, arguably New Zealand's most complete wine region, from Bordeaux blends to coastal Chardonnay.
climate: Warm, maritime
fact: Gimblett Gravels, often seen as the premier area, sits 15 km from the Pacific.

video.title: Merlot (Everything you need to know) | Grapes 101

pageType: section of the NZ Chardonnay article
description: Chardonnay with bright stone fruit and a mineral core, alongside world-class Pinot Noir.
climate: Cooler, free-draining soils
fact: The best Martinborough Chardonnays improve with bottle age.

video.title: Whoa! New Zealand Chardonnay

pageType: section of the NZ Chardonnay article
description: One of the world's premier regions for truly cool-climate Chardonnay: clean, ripe fruit with fresh acidity.
climate: Long dry summers, the Nor'wester, cool nights
fact: Limestone soils give the best wines elegance and minerality.

video.title: Whoa! New Zealand Chardonnay

pageType: dedicated (country page)
description: Old and New World winemaking meet. A warm climate and ancient granite soils give bold, aromatic reds and whites.
climate: Warm
fact: 'Estate Wines' come from registered vineyards farmed as one unit (207 in total).

video.title: Hunting Syrah in South Africa

pageType: dedicated article
description: South Africa's most developed winelands and the centre of wine tourism, likened to Napa for California.
fact: Top wines come from granite mountain soils about 600 million years old, over 3x as old as Napa's.

video.title: Cabernet Sauvignon (Everything You Need To Know) | Grapes 101

pageType: video page (thin)
description: South African Syrah, 'an absolute find'.

video.title: Hunting Syrah in South Africa

pageType: dedicated article
description: British Columbia region whose best wines are dry reds and whites. Desert-like hills to cool lakeside benches, now 11 sub-GIs.
climate: Dry, sunny, hot, short season; lake-moderated
fact: Severe winters periodically kill vines to the root, so they regrow new trunks.
